chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who becomes Muslim and intends to perform Hajj, and the season for Hajj has presented itself: should he perform Hajj or be circumcised? He (peace be upon him) said: He should not perform Hajj until he is circumcised.

key_terms.حَضَرَ الْحَجُّ: the Hajj season presented itself / arrived

ai.seo_question: Does a new Muslim convert need to be circumcised before performing Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for a new male convert, circumcision is a prerequisite for the validity of his Hajj, requiring him to delay the pilgrimage until the ritual is completed. This ruling underscores the integration of physical purity (*taharah*) with ritual validity in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing the obligations of new converts from those who have been Muslim since birth. The emphasis on completing this fundamental act of entering the fold of Islam before undertaking the major pilgrimage highlights the sequential nature of religious duties for initiates.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibrahim Bin Maymoun,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who became a Muslim, so he intended to perform Hajj, and the (season) for the Hajj had presented itself, should he perform Hajj or should he be circumcised?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should not perform Hajj until he is circumcised’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Ibrahim ibn Maymun who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who becomes a Muslim and wants to perform al-Hajj and it is time for al-Hajj, if he performs al-Hajj or circumcision.
He (the Imam) said, ‘He must not perform al-Hajj until he is circumcised.”’
